Subject: Follow-up: Deployment path & data isolation checklist

Tom/Leah — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap and the asks we captured on the call so we have a single source of truth before the procurement thread starts.

What we heard:
- Primary requirement: strict data isolation for PHI/PII workloads. Team prefers a deployment that ensures network and key custody separation.
- Preferred outcome: Private VPC (control plane in customer VPC / private control plane) is ideal from a compliance standpoint, but procurement timeline may push you toward Dedicated capacity if we can guarantee KMS/keys and audit evidence.
- Hard blockers: customer-managed KMS or BYOK; per-tenant network policies; signed retention & delete SLA; SOC2 report and relevant pen-test evidence.

Open questions / asks (for Redwood & CuraTech):
1) Can Redwood enable customer-managed keys for Dedicated deployments or is BYOK only available for Private?
2) What level of network isolation (subnet/VPC peering, private endpoint, ingress firewall) do we need documented for procurement?
3) Can we get an estimate for a minimal BOM (GPU count / expected monthly committed spend) for a 3-month PoC in Dedicated vs Private?

Attachments: redwood-deploy-matrix.xlsx (draft mapping of features ↔ deployment modes), curatech_pci_questions.pdf (your questionnaire from today)

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik to share a short technical comparison (Dedicated vs Private) with explicit answers about KMS and audit logs.
- Proposal of dates for a 30-min ops workshop next week to align on network/VPC specifics and BOM.
- I'll open the HubSpot deal and drop the draft MOA for legal if we want to speed procurement.

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll coordinate the workshop time with Karthik and Ben.

Tom/Team — following our discussion, here is a compact technical comparison and direct answers to the three asks Jasmine listed. I kept it focused to support procurement.

Dedicated (reserved GPU pool, Redwood-managed control plane) — what we can deliver quickly:
- KMS/BYOK: Available under Enterprise package. Customer supplies key material via standard KMS APIs; keys are deployed to HSM-backed key stores and used for dataset-at-rest encryption. Control plane retains minimal metadata, crypto material never leaves HSM.
- Audit logs: Token-level call traces, model invocation logs, and per-request latency/cost metadata available. We can provide retention exports (immutable) for up to 12 months and a daily S3 export if you want immutable copies.
- Network: Private endpoints + VPC peering available; Dedicated instances can be deployed in private subnets with no public egress.

Private VPC (customer-run control plane / VPC-hosted) — maximum isolation:
- KMS/BYOK: Full customer control; KMS/HSM integration in your VPC. Keys never traverse Redwood control plane.
- Audit logs: Logs stay in your logging stack (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/S3) per your retention policies.
- Network: Network completely inside customer VPC; optional on-prem bridging is supported.

Trade-offs & recommended short path for PoC:
- If procurement needs the legal comfort of key custody AND you need a tight timeline, we recommend Dedicated with BYOK + daily immutable log export (we can provide an audited runbook and a SOC2 supplement) — this shortens setup by ~2–4 weeks versus a Private VPC install.
- If you need absolute control (keys never touched by Redwood), Private VPC is the correct long-term solution — procurement paperwork will take longer and require network ops involvement.

BOM estimate for a small PoC (3 months):
- Dedicated: 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved), expected committed spend ~$45k/mo (estimate depends on concurrency & context lengths)
- Private VPC: additional engineering integration fees for control plane deployment and on-prem networking — expect +4–6 weeks and ~$60k–80k one-time infra/eng setup depending on region and HSM procurement.

Files: redwood-deploy-matrix.xlsx (attached) — I flagged exact feature parity and where we need customer ops input.

If that sounds right, I can block a 30-minute ops + procurement workshop (Karthik + Ben + Jasmine + CuraTech security/procurement) next week.
